newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilectra to invest $250 mln abroad 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chilectra to invest $250 mln abroad 1997.

text.p: Chile's largest electricity distributor Chilectra plans to invest $250 million this year in power companies it owns in Argentina, Brazil and Peru, said general manager Marcos Zylberberg.
The company will invest $110 million in Edesur in Buenos Aires, $100 million in Rio de Janeiro distributor CERJ and $45 million in Lima-based Edelnor, he told a news conference.
Chilectra will also spend 19 billion pesos in Santiago this year, up 11 percent on its investment in the city last year.
"This increase is due to the high rates of growth in electricity demand in the Metropolitan Region, which we estimate to be between 7.5 and 8 percent this year," said Zylberberg.
Chilectra is around 75-percent owned by power investment company Enersis.
The company's local investments, which include four new substations, will be financed from its own resources.

The investments in the foreign companies, which are owned by consortia including Chilectra, Enersis and other partners, will be financed from various sources and not necessarily from Chilectra's own funds, he said.
Chilectra will invest $860 million abroad over the next five years and $1.1 billion in Santiago. ((-- Paulina Modiano, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212))
